# Vacuum-salt plant, vapour recompression evaporator: data sheet

REAL DESIGN DATA from US Patent 5,366,514 (Texas Brine Corp., 1994), FIG. 1 and Table I: a 2,500 short-ton-per-day
plant making 99.99 % NaCl from solution-mined brine. The drawing is the patent's FIG. 1; numbers in brackets are the
patent's reference numerals. Equipment ratings marked ILLUSTRATIVE are not in the patent.

## Operating point (patent Table I, converted to SI)
| Stream / item | Value |
|---|---|
| Feed brine to the brine cooled condenser (3) (stream 2), "saturated in salt" (about 26 wt % NaCl) | 362.9 t/h at 24 °C |
| Brine leaving the brine cooled condenser | 60 °C |
| Elutriating brine to the evaporator legs (streams 7, 8) | 98.0 t/h at 60 °C |
| Brine through the brine preheater BP (10) to the VRC evaporator (12) (streams 9/11) | 264.9 t/h, 60 → 125.6 °C |
| VRC evaporator (12) | 1.70 bar(a) (10 psig), brine boiling at 125.6 °C |
| VRC evaporator overhead to the VRC compressor (26) (stream 25) | 226.8 t/h steam, saturation 115.2 °C at 1.70 bar(a) |
| VRC compressor (26) discharge | 3.08 bar(a) (30 psig), pressure ratio 1.8 |
| Desuperheated steam to the circulating heater CH1 (stream 36), incl. 15.9 t/h turbine exhaust (stream 33) | 251.7 t/h at 135 °C, 3.08 bar(a) |
| CH1 condensate (stream 21) | 251.7 t/h at 134.4 °C, cooled in BP (10) to about 82 °C |
| Excess VRC evaporator vapour to the purge heater CH2 (stream 31) | 20.9 t/h |
| Purge liquor, VRC evaporator → purge evaporator (5) (stream 14) | 47.6 t/h at 125.6 °C |
| Purge evaporator (5) | about 1.01 bar(a), 108.9 °C |
| Purge to the disposal well facility (18) (stream 16) | 6.8 t/h at 108.9 °C |
| Purge-evaporator overheads to the brine cooled condenser (stream 4) | 25.4 t/h at 100.6 °C after desuperheating |
| Salt produced (dry) (17) | 94.9 t/h (2,511 short t/d) |

The patent describes the FIG. 1 feed as "saturated in salt". It explicitly allows lower-concentration feed; solution-mined
brine can arrive below saturation. Use `feed_x_NaCl` to examine that case rather than treating 26 wt % as universal.

## What the patent says about the equipment
- The VRC compressor (26) is a single-wheel centrifugal compressor, 1.8:1, driven by the combustion gas turbine (37). "The VRC
  compressor can only pass a fixed amount of steam": the vapour above its suction capacity (about 90 % of the boil-up passes
  it) is the excess sent to the purge evaporator heater CH2 (patent col. 7-8).
- Desuperheating condensate is sprayed into the compressor discharge because superheated steam transfers heat poorly in the
  large circulating heaters (col. 7). The desuperheater is not drawn in FIG. 1.

## Equipment ratings
- VRC compressor (26) suction capacity: 226.8 t/h (the patent's fixed compressor throughput). Shaft power: not stated in the patent.
- Circulating heater CH1: 8,800 m², U 2,000 W/m²K in service (ILLUSTRATIVE; 2,500 W/m²K clean).
- Forced-circulation pump of the VRC evaporator (not drawn in FIG. 1): 15,000 m³/h rated (ILLUSTRATIVE).
- Purge heater CH2: 1,500 m², U 1,500 W/m²K (ILLUSTRATIVE).

## Process requirements and design rules
- Brine temperature rise through CH1 at most 3 K: a larger rise flashes in the tubes and scales them with salt.
- Condensate leaves CH1 saturated at the shell pressure.
- The brine boils above the steam saturation temperature by its boiling point elevation (use the brine_bpe tool).

## Modelling scope (from the plant's process engineer)
- The capacity question is decided by the VRC loop: VRC evaporator (12) boil-up, VRC compressor (26), the discharge
  desuperheating and the circulating heater CH1, plus the purge evaporator (5) with CH2 that takes the excess vapour.
  Model that loop in detail.
- The feed preheat train (brine cooled condenser, BP) is not in question: take the brine entering the VRC evaporator from
  Table I (264.9 t/h at 125.6 °C, plus 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 °C, both scaling with throughput) instead of
  closing the condensate-to-brine heat-recovery loops.
- Turbine exhaust steam joining the compressor discharge (stream 33): 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a), fixed (the gas turbine does
  not grow with salt production).

## Request
Sales wants the plant to make **3,000 short tons per day instead of 2,500 (+20 %)**.

submit.label: as-built-base
assumptions: Water stand-in (Steam Tables IAPWS-IF97) with evaporator feed_x_NaCl salt balance and Sparrow BPE per run_process evaporator description; electrolyte phase equilibria omitted, so stream T is water saturation and brine boiling temperature is the unit brine_T_C.

Data-sheet Modelling scope governs over full P&ID topology for the as-built question: feed preheat train (BCC-1, BP-1, CST-1, BPF-1) is not solved; VRE feed is taken as boundary feeds S11 = 264.9 t/h at 125.6 C plus S7 = 98.0 t/h elutriating brine at 60 C, both from data sheet Table I rows. Condensate-to-brine recovery connections 9, 21, 22, 24 and brine connections 2, 19 are therefore boundary flows, not closed loops.

Closed CH1 steam loop is unfolded once-through per instructions: utility feed S36 = 251.7 t/h at 135 C, 3.08 bar(a) (data sheet row, stream 36) drives VRE-1 heating and leaves as S21_COND condensate; it is not recycled. The compressor discharge return is solved separately through mixer MX-DESH to terminal stream S36_RETURN as a desuperheating check.

Turbine exhaust S33 is a fixed utility feed (utility:true, does not scale): 15.9 t/h at 3.08 bar(a) from data sheet row; its temperature is not stated in the data sheet and is assumed 135 C (equal to the desuperheated steam temperature) - stated assumption, not a measured value.

Desuperheater is not drawn on FIG. 1 (data sheet note) and is modelled as mixer MX-DESH; spray SPRAY = 14.0 t/h condensate at 134.4 C (CH1 condensate temperature, data sheet row stream 21) calibrated in run as-built-base so the mixer outlet S36_RETURN is saturated at 134.43 C. Spray rate itself is not a Table I measured value.

CH1 is included in VRE-1 and CH2 in PE-1 (P&ID equipment notes: VRE-1 'includes CH1', PE-1 'includes CH2'); there are no separate CH1/CH2 P&ID tags, so heater area/U limits are placed on VRE-1/PE-1. Ratings are the data-sheet ILLUSTRATIVE ratings used exactly as given, never raised: CH1 8,800 m2 U 2,000 W/m2K in service, CH2 1,500 m2 U 1,500 W/m2K.

VRC-1 efficiency 75% is an assumed value only to estimate shaft duty (patent states shaft power not stated, data sheet Equipment ratings); discharge pressure 3.08 bar(a) and suction capacity 226.8 t/h are data-sheet values. Compressor discharge temperature is therefore not a calibrated measurement.

Splitter fractions are calibration parameters, not equipment ratings: VRE liquid purge fraction 0.378 calibrated to Table I purge 47.6 t/h; VRE vapour excess fraction 0.0843 = Table I ratio 20.9/(226.8+20.9); PE liquid disposal fraction 0.247 calibrated to Table I disposal 6.8 t/h.
Salt product streams S13_SALT and S20_SALT are water-stand-in liquid (crystals plus mother liquor); the dry salt rate is the sum of the evaporator salt_kg_h outputs, not the stream kg/h.

Cogeneration and downstream items CGT-1, HRSG-1, ST-1, GEN-1, SRP-1, DWF-1, CST-1 carry no process ratings in the P&ID (all capacity_kW/flow_gpm null) or data sheet and are represented only by their boundary streams (S33 turbine exhaust in; S13/S20 salt out; S15 disposal out); GEN-1 is electrical only.

Forced-circulation pump is not drawn in FIG. 1 and its 15,000 m3/h rating is ILLUSTRATIVE with no Table I circulation flow, head or temperature-rise measurement; the CH1 brine rise <=3 K rule therefore cannot be checked in this spec and is not represented as a limit - no rating was invented for it.

P&ID data_quality/read_notes state no capacities, flows or valve types are printed and connections use reference numerals 1-37; all values therefore come from the data sheet Table I/ratings, and P&ID printed evaporator conditions (10 PSIG 258F = 1.70 bar(a)/125.6 C; 0 PSIG 228F = 1.01 bar(a)/108.9 C) agree with the data sheet - no P&ID-vs-datasheet conflict was found. Patent Table I is not exactly heat-closed: with Table I heating steam the simulator boil-up is heat-limited below Table I vapour/salt rates; deviations are reported in calibration, not hidden by raising any rating.
